This is, if not one of the greatest games of all time, absolutely outstanding. I've already played TLOU2 on PS5 but I instantly bought when it came to PC because I had such a great experience with it and the PC version is no different in that regard. Unlike the Part 1 release on PC, I've had 0 issues with the port-- it runs beautifully.

As for the actual game, it has some of the best, most fluid gameplay I've ever experienced (which feels SO much better on a keyboard and mouse), top tier graphics, (and despite what an ignorant, highly vocal minority says) an amazing story that genuinely makes you FEEL something and there's a lot of content and fun to be had in No Return after beating the story. There's a lot of replay value as well despite being totally linear. If you're going to play this game, which EVERYONE should, play part 1 first. It's necessary to understand the events of this game.

Feels a lot like the first one. I don't feel, like many have suggested, that the LGBT stuff is really "forced down your throat" in this title and I hate that shit. That said, I'm a member of the community myself and it's nice to see that stuff from time to time, but I hate it when it's shoehorned in. 

ANYWAYS, gorgeous game. Runs really well on my PC. Plays a lot like the first game. Basically more of the same, but more story. If you liked the first game, you'll like this one. If you're unfamiliar totally, get the first game. It still holds up in 2026.

I, like so many of you, bought this game day 1 on PS4. Back then, I could not bring myself to finish this story. I was so frustrated with Druckmann's decisions, such as being forced to play as Abby, Joel's cold-blooded killer. 5 years later I decided to give this game another try and I am so glad I did that. This time I knew what to expect and my initial disappointments were in the background.

What we get is a deep exploration of revenge and morality. Yes, it turns out revenge can and will be messy. 5 years ago, I was simply not prepared for how emotionally taxing this game would be. This time, I made it my goal to complete the game no matter what. I am so glad that I did. This game is bleaker and darker than the first entry. While I did not sit in my chair with my jaw hanging open by the time the credits rolled (the way I did in TLOS: Part 1), this story affected me on a deep level. This game is a roller coaster of emotions and it will stay with me forever. Do yourself a favor and play this game. 9.5/10

I bought it and tried it out. The gameplay is great, the mechanics and gunplay and a few new added features make it feel smoother than TLOU 1. However, I just found the game to be boring and repetitive. Playing as Ellie was fun in the beginning then towards the end of her arch it started to feel rinse and repeat. By the time you play as Abby there's nothing new, just the same search for loot and kill everything. The story and writing just feels blah and Im not interested. I feel like they shoulda kept Joel and Ellie and wrote a narrative around them and left this Abby storyline out of it. Her and her friends I didnt care for and I just wanted to play as Joel and Ellie. Couldnt finish the game halfway through Abbys play through.

I'd like to say these things but I can't, because the game is broken. Regular graphics driver crashes on a very reliable 7600XT system (that plays all other games without a single issue on max settings). Random crashes. Guaranteed crashes on certain cutscenes. And a developer that clearly can't be bothered to fix these issues, because they've existed for months, identified by thousands of players online. This isn't an AMD problem either, because Nvidia cards suffer the exact same issues.

So yeah, don't buy this game for Windows. Get it on a PS5 or similar, but don't bother with the PC port because it isn't worth the hassle.

The Last of Us es una de mis franquicias favoritas. En Part 1, termine encantado por la historia de Joel siendo un hombre roto volviendo a encontrar la luz gracias a Ellie. En Part 2, termine con una sensación difícil de describir, fue una historia cruda, sin final feliz y con el tan mencionado "ciclo de la violencia". El gameplay es muy entretenido, los diálogos entre personajes siguen siendo los mejores en la industria y la ambientación muestra el nivel de detalle que maneja Naughty Dog.

La única diferencia entre a alguien que le encanto este juego y alguien que lo odia, es si logra empatizar con Abby.

This game was surrounded by a huge amount of controversy when it came out, but I've gotta say, this is the best game I have ever played. I would rate it a 10/10, the story was incredibly sad, but also quite thought provoking and while playing I also stopped multiple times just to admire the beauty of this game. Unlike some other games, I'm looking at you Black Myth Wukong, I could actually run this game at ~90 fps at max settings, without FSR too! The gameplay is buttery smooth, the story is amazing, the graphics are beautiful, and most of all the acting is the best I've ever seen in a video game.
11/10

The emotional turmoil of this game can't be understated. I think a lot of people may not like where this game takes them, and I think that's fair. But if you want an incredible experience that forces you to face things you've probably not felt playing other games before, this is it.

Adding to that, visually this is probably the most beautiful game I've ever played and that alone makes it worth experiencing to me. The voice acting and characters are all amazing. Gameplay, combat all feel so smooth and enjoyable. I loved every minute of this game, even when I kinda hated what it was putting me through.

I've heard criticism about this game's pacing, and yes, the thirty-ish hours it will take to complete your first playthrough might in the moment feel a bit drawn out, especially as several levels boil down to "traverse this area to go somewhere else."

That said however, the thought of more content being left on the cutting room floor, missing out on levels the developers made for me - i couldn't bear that. I don't want anything taken away from me, not in this game, not a single second. And after the credits rolled, i was gutted that it was over. There wasn't anything more of this merciless, tortorous descent into the eternal poison that is violence, I felt empty, following all the emotional tolls the characters had to suffer through. And i was still gutted that the first playthough was over, the story having unfolded, no surprises and twists left to experience for the first time. 

That is about the highest praise i can think of.

Finally, it's here on PC. The Last of Us Part 2 is better than the first, more mature and complex in terms of the story and its themes, plus a lot of subtlety I've seen people miss about characters, story, and subtext. Naughty Dog was bold and unapologetic, how art should be. Gameplay is more fluid and refined, while level design is way more open and better than TLOU 1. I think it's one of the more underrated games of the last decade; as such, it divided the fanbase—you either love it or hate it. That means the game stuck to its guns and didn't compromise on its vision, which to me is a sign of integrity. I recommend it, no doubt.
